title: Count Subarrays With Exactly k Bad Days

description.intro:
Given an array, sales, where sales[i] is the number of sales on day i, count the number of subarrays with exactly k bad days.

A bad day is a day with fewer than 10 sales.
examples:
Example 1: sales = [0, 20, 5], k = 1
Output: 4
The subarrays [0], [0, 20], [20, 5], and [5] have 1 bad day each.

Example 2: sales = [10, 20, 30], k = 1
Output: 0
No subarrays have exactly 1 bad day.

Example 3: sales = [0, 5, 8], k = 2
Output: 2
The subarrays [0, 5] and [5, 8] have exactly 2 bad days.
description.approach:
There is a trick to reduce "Exactly-K" counting problems to "At-Most-K" counting problems:

If k == 0, "at most 0" and "exactly 0" are the same.
For k > 0, the number of subarrays with exactly k bad days is equal to the number of subarrays with at most k bad days minus the number of subarrays with at most k - 1 bad days.
For example, this figure shows an example sales array and all 16 subarrays with at most 2 bad days. Of those, 10 have at most 1 bad day, meaning there are 16 - 10 = 6 subarrays with exactly 2 bad days. By the same logic, there are 10 - 2 = 8 subarrays with exactly 1 bad day.

Count Subarrays With Exactly K Bad Days Solution
![alt text](image-5.png)
So, if we want to count subarrays with exactly 2 bad days, we can:

Count all subarrays with at most 2 bad days (meaning 0, 1, or 2 bad days)
Count all subarrays with at most 1 bad day (meaning 0 or 1 bad day)
Subtract the second count from the first count

complexity:
Time & Space Analysis
n: the length of the sales array

k: the maximum number of bad days allowed

Time: O(2 * n) = O(n) - each of the two at-most-k subproblems takes O(n) time: we increment a pointer at each iteration, so there are at most 2n iterations

Extra space: O(1)

tests.python:
def run_tests():
  tests = [
      # Example from the book
      ([0, 20, 5], 1, 4),
      # Edge case - empty array
      ([], 1, 0),
      # Edge case - k = 0
      ([0, 20, 5], 0, 1),
      # Edge case - all good days
      ([10, 20, 30], 1, 0),
      # Edge case - all bad days
      ([0, 5, 8], 2, 2),
  ]
  for sales, k, want in tests:
    got = count_exactly_k_bad_days(sales, k)
    assert got == want, f"\ncount_exactly_k_bad_days({sales}, {k}): got: {        got}, want: {want}\n"

run_tests()
